Method of Attack: Typosquatting popular Lodash library to trick developers
Contains base64-obfuscated code that launches a bundled 'dataset.db' file which is a tainted Windows AnyDesk executable
Creates a Google directory in APPDATA, copies AnyDesk executable renamed as Chrome.exe, and executes it to establish remote access
Attack Vector: Malicious npm package installation via typosquatting
Indicators of Compromise: Package names similar to Lodash but with version 4.17.24 (vs Lodash 4.17.21)
Bundled 'dataset.db' file which is actually a Windows EXE (AnyDesk.exe)
Execution of Chrome.exe renamed AnyDesk binary in APPDATA\Google directory
Code signing certificate from 'philandro Software GmbH' dated April 7, 2020
References in legitimate package READMEs (e.g., restrict-imports-loader) lending false credibility
